posts.name: Plunder Skol
posts.cooked:
Hello everyone, PEA evolved to the point where I decided to rename it PEARL and establish it as a stable hub for the tools I use most while playing EVE Online.

PEARL is an open-source Windows desktop application designed mainly for players who buy, manage and run EVE Online escalations at scale.

Main features include:

  • Monitoring configured market chatlogs and detecting escalation offers.
  • Custom sound alerts for market offers, hostile intel and expiring escalations.
  • Active escalation timers, purchase prices, expenses, loot and total profit tracking.
  • Interactive regional maps with Intel, zKill activity, Danger Zones and character locations.
  • Stargate, jump-drive and hybrid route planning with Ansiblex support and fuel estimates.
  • ESI character tracking, waypoint delivery and EVE Mail import/export packages.
  • Integrated multibox client previews, configurable hotkeys, hotswap order and support for external windows.
  • Cyno, jump route and accessible Pharolux assistance.
  • Integrated Pathfinder directly with PEARL, allowing both tools to cross-reference information
  • tax and reimbursement information in automatic EVE Mail receipts.
  • Added recursive Manufacturing and Reaction planning down to base resources.
  • Mining planner for asteroids, Ice, gas and Moons (this one omg its great)

PEARL was inspired by SMT and EVE-O Preview, but was developed with tools tailored to my own more specific needs.

SMT is a much broader and more established mapping, Intel and navigation tool. PEARL takes inspiration from it, but focuses primarily on the complete escalation workflow: detecting offers, purchasing them, managing timers, planning routes and tracking investment and profit.

EVE-O Preview is a specialized and mature client preview/window switcher. PEARL includes a preview system inside the same application, but combines it with escalation management, maps, Intel, routing and financial tracking.

Credits

A special thank you to Slazanger, creator of SMT, and to the EVE-O Preview team: StinkRay, Devilen, Dal Shooth, Izakbar, Aura Asuna, Phrynohyas Tig-Rah, Makari Aeron and CCP FoxFour.

PEARL was only possible because these projects demonstrated what community-made EVE tools could achieve.

The application is portable and open source. The executable is currently unsigned, so Windows may display a SmartScreen or Defender warning.

PEA 0.5.3 is now available!

This update focuses on quality of life, performance and reliability.

What’s new:

  • Added EVE Mail export/import, making it easy to back up and share your escalation database between characters.

  • Improved route planning and fuel calculations.

  • Better UI responsiveness and general performance optimizations.

  • Multiple bug fixes and stability improvements.

  • Various usability tweaks based on community feedback.

Thanks to everyone who has been testing the app and sending suggestions. Keep the feedback coming, it has been extremely helpful and continues to shape the project.

posts.name: Plunder Skol
posts.cooked:
I just added an industry manager in update 0.9.4, because why not?

I’m going to ask some of my corp mates to test it because I’m definitely not a hardcore industry guy. I mostly build Typhoons and other simple stuff, but I’ll do my best to turn this into a solid industry calculator.

It can already break production down into the base materials you need, including reaction materials, asteroid minerals, PI, and other raw resources. Right now I’m improving the manufacturing side for modules, components, and intermediate parts.

It’s already good enough for a small-scale industry guy like me, but I’m really excited about where this can go, so I’ll keep working on it and try to make it a genuinely useful industry tool.

PEARL 1.0.6 focuses primarily on improving the stability and reliability of the Preview/Multibox system.

The Preview window switching system was extensively audited after detecting cases where Windows foreground activation could stall for several seconds and temporarily interfere with normal mouse and keyboard input.
